description: Four small populations drifting at random: each island resamples its allele frequency every generation under selection, mutation and migration, and puts the four frequencies out as bounded CV.

params.text: Sets the number of allele copies in each island, 8 to 4096 on a log2 scale; more copies make each random step smaller and smoother.
Sets the signed fitness advantage, -0.25 to +0.25; below centre favours allele B and above it favours allele A.
Sets the symmetric mutation probability per copy per generation: exactly zero at the bottom, then 0.000001 to 0.05 on a logarithmic scale.
Sets the fraction of each island replaced from the common migrant pool, 0 to 1; at 1 every island starts a generation from the same probability.
Sets the internal generation rate, stopped at the bottom and then exponential up to 200 generations a second.
Resamples the next island in the repeating order 1, 2, 3, 4 from eight copies only, which it holds until the next ordinary generation redraws it at the SIZE setting.
Returns all four islands and the event memory to the deterministic starting state.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the selection.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the mutation probability.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the migration fraction.

inputs.text: Doubles the allele-copy count for every volt, added to the SIZE knob and clamped to 8 through 4096 copies.
Modulates the selection, 0.05 per volt through its attenuverter.
Modulates the mutation probability along its logarithmic scale, a tenth of the knob's range per volt through its attenuverter.
Modulates the migration fraction, a tenth per volt through its attenuverter.
Doubles the running generation rate for every volt, added to the GENERATIONS knob and capped at 200 generations a second.
A rising edge past 1V advances exactly one synchronous generation, without resetting the phase of the internal clock.
A rising edge past 1V bottlenecks the next island in rotation to eight copies.
A rising edge past 1V restores the initial population and clears the event memory.

outputs.text: The allele-A frequency of that island, 0 to 10V.
The mean allele-A frequency across the four islands, 0 to 10V.
The within-island heterozygosity, 0 to 10V: 10V when every island is at a frequency of a half, and 0V when every island is internally fixed, including when the four are split between all-A and all-B.
10V for as long as every island is fixed at allele A.
10V for as long as every island is fixed at allele B.
A 10V pulse 1ms long on entry into either global fixation state.
A 10V pulse 1ms long when the mean frequency enters the A-high or the B-high region.

notes: With the generation rate at the bottom the simulation is stopped, and nothing changes until a trigger arrives at STEP; the two can also be used together.
Changing a knob never redraws the population already on screen; a new setting only alters the probabilities of the generations that follow.
The five frequency and heterozygosity outputs ramp to each new generation's value over 50ms rather than stepping, so they can be patched to audio-rate destinations without clicking.
The screen plots the recent history of the four island frequencies, with a ring marking the island the next founder bottleneck will hit.
menu: New random seed — replaces the random stream the simulation draws from, so the sequence from here on differs.
Restore factory seed — returns the random stream to the one the module ships with, making the sequence repeatable.
